'''''Thunbergia mysorensis''''', the '''Mysore trumpetvine'''<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}}</ref> or '''lady's slipper vine''',<ref name="RFK">{{cite web |author1=F.A.Zich |author2=B.P.M.Hyland |author3=T.Whiffen |author4=R.A.Kerrigan |author2-link=Bernard Hyland |year=2020 |url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/rainforest/text/entities/Thunbergia_mysorensis.htm |title=''Thunbergia mysorensis'' |website=[[Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants]] Edition 8 (RFK8) |publisher=Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research (CANBR), [[Australian Government]] |access-date=27 June 2021}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Acanthaceae. A woody-stemmed [[evergreen]], this [[liana|vine]] is native to southern tropical India.<ref name="uconn">[http://titanarum.uconn.edu/199900057.html Univ. Connecticut plant treatment: ''Thunbergia mysorensis'' {Acanthaceae} Clock Vine] . accessed 5.1.2011</ref> The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''mysorensis'' is derived from the city of [[Mysore]].<ref name="uconn"/>

==Description==
''Thunbergia mysorensis'' often reaches {{convert|6|m|ft}} and has long narrow medium green leaves.  The dramatic and very large pendent hanging blossoms have individual flowers in a bold curved shape. This is enhanced by their being a rich saturated yellow, with maroon to brownish red outer tip coloring.<ref name="uconn"/> The vine blooms from spring to autumn.<ref name="uconn"/>

==Cultivation==
''Thunbergia mysorensis'' is cultivated as a popular [[ornamental plant]] in tropical and sub-tropical gardens, conservatories and [[greenhouse]]s.<ref name="uconn"/> It grows quickly in frost-free temperate climates, such as coastal [[Southern California]], with flowers draping down from [[pergola]]s and other garden structures.<ref>[http://www.californiagardens.com/Plant_Pages/thunbergia_mysorensis.htm California_Gardens: ''Thunbergia mysorensis'' - Brick and Butter Vine info page] . accessed 5.1.2011</ref> Its sweet nectar is attractive to [[sunbird]]s, a very small [[passerine]] bird, and [[hummingbird]]s.<ref name="uconn"/> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Thunbergia mysorensis '' | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/18176/Thunbergia-mysorensis/Details | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 102 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 23 December 2018}}</ref>
